title: Drop after drop
category: descriptive rhythmic formula; dictionary-labelled Dhaga, not a moral proverb
explanation: The repeated ending lets the ear follow separate drops. Unlike a moral saying, this short formula describes an action through sound. The source explicitly glosses juice falling drop by drop. Our reading enjoys the playful rhythm without adding a lesson about people or claiming a particular performance tradition.
meaning_odia: ଥପଂ ଥପଂର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ ଟୋପା ପରେ ଟୋପା ପଡ଼ିବାର ଲୟ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ମଧ୍ୟ କୌଣସି ଦ୍ରବ୍ୟରୁ ଟୋପା ଟୋପା ରସ ଗଳିବା ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଏଠି ଶବ୍ଦର ଖେଳ ଗୋଟିଏ କ୍ରିୟାକୁ ଶୁଣାଏ; ମଣିଷ ପାଇଁ ନୀତିବାକ୍ୟ ତିଆରି କରେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଲୟର ରସଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ।
english_summary: A descriptive sound-play formula follows juice falling drop by drop.
odia_summary: ଟୋପା ଟୋପା ରସ ଗଳିବାକୁ ଶବ୍ଦର ଲୟ ଅନୁସରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: While squeezing a cut orange over a bowl, a reader watches the last drops fall and playfully says the line in time with them. The orange and this conversation are invented; the source names no particular fruit or occasion.
cultural_context: The dictionary labels it Dhaga, but the supplied gloss is descriptive. Treat it as language play, not a popular standalone proverb or an attested moral.94315 remains a possible alias awaiting full comparison.
